sections.name: File setup, params
sections.title: Test setup and helpers
sections.what: Loads the test tools, the extraction route handlers, and the document service. Defines a helper that builds the route parameters.
sections.why: Same reason as the other route tests: route handlers take their parameters as a promise.
sections.watch_out: The helper must produce the same parameter shape the route expects.

sections.name: synthetic extraction boundary
sections.title: Cross-case and no-provider tests
sections.what: The first test checks that a document belonging to another case is refused before any AI call. The second test checks that with no provider set, the route returns a safe unavailable response and restores the environment afterward.
sections.why: Protects case data and makes the unavailable state predictable.
sections.watch_out: If you add tests that change environment settings, keep the restore step or they will affect other tests.

summary: Tests that document extraction refuses cross-case access and returns a safe unavailable response when no AI provider is configured.
purpose: Protects the extraction feature from misuse and from calling an outside AI service by accident.
why: Likely reason: extraction can send document text to an outside AI provider, so these checks keep that controlled.
how: The first test asks for a document from a different case and expects 404 on both GET and POST. The second test removes the AI provider settings, calls POST, expects 503 with code AI_UNAVAILABLE, and then restores the original settings.
inputs: Demo case and document ids. Environment settings for AI provider keys.
outputs: Pass or fail for each test.
risks: The second test changes global environment settings. The restore step runs in a finally block, which protects against leftover changes after a failure.
debug: If the second test fails, check how the extraction code picks a provider and which environment settings it reads.
